Placeholders are resolved at runtime by `interpolateUrl()` in the navigation package of `openmrs-esm-core`. It substitutes `${openmrsBase}` and `${openmrsSpaBase}` from the page's globals, then any extra parameters the caller passes. It is not a build-time step. The docs in `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs` describe this behaviour, and the app shell and login app call it wherever a configured URL is used.

**Implementation**

- `interpolateUrl()` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-navigation/src/navigation/interpolate-string.ts:37-48`) reads `window.getOpenmrsSpaBase()` with its trailing slash trimmed, and `window.openmrsBase`. It merges these with any `additionalParams` and calls `interpolateString`. It then collapses a leading `//` that interpolation can create (for example `/${openmrsSpaBase}` becoming `//openmrs/spa`), unless the template itself started with `//`.
- `interpolateString()` (same file, lines 66-69) does a plain split-and-join for each `${key}`. Unknown placeholders are left as they are.
- `navigate()` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-navigation/src/navigation/navigate.ts:50-64`) calls `interpolateUrl(to, templateParams)` first. It then only uses in-app `navigateToUrl` when the target starts with the SPA base, and falls back to `window.location.assign` otherwise. It rejects non-http(s) targets.
- Config loading (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/run.ts:257-261`) interpolates each entry in `configUrls` before fetching it. The loaded config is keyed by the original, uninterpolated string.
- Components that take configured URLs also call it, including the logo (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-login-app/src/logo.component.tsx`), the login background (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-login-app/src/login-page-wrapper/login-page-wrapper.component.tsx:34`) and `ConfigurableLink` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/ConfigurableLink.tsx:69`).
- Config validation accepts only `openmrsBase`, `openmrsSpaBase` and any parameters the schema declares. The check is `isUrlWithTemplateParameters` (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-config/src/validators/validators.ts:23-41`).

**Documentation**

- `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs/content/en-US/docs/configure-o3/overview.mdx:369` says `configUrls` entries are interpolated at runtime with `interpolateUrl()`, and gives `${openmrsSpaBase}/config.json` → `/openmrs/spa/config.json`.
- `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs/content/en-US/docs/configure-o3/configure-branding.mdx:205-212` covers the `image` template variables.
- `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs/content/en-US/docs/configure-o3/configure-patient-management.mdx:711` and `configure-service-queues.mdx:354` list the supported placeholders for their URL templates.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/interpolateUrl.md` and `docs/functions/navigate.md` are the generated API docs for the same functions.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/tooling/openmrs/README.md:213` says `configUrls` can use `${openmrsSpaBase}`, which the app fills in with the SPA path.

**Not verified**

- I did not read where `window.getOpenmrsSpaBase` and `window.openmrsBase` are set. The only match I found is a call at `openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/index.ts:86`.
- I did not check the frontend `startup.sh` substitution mentioned in the overview docs, which is a separate Docker-time mechanism for `$SPA_PATH`-style placeholders.

363: **Important**: Changes to `spa-build-config.json` require rebuilding the frontend SPA to take effect. The `openmrs build` command reads this file as literal JSON and does not expand shell environment variables. Runtime environment overrides are a Reference Application Docker pattern handled by its frontend `startup.sh` script after the SPA has been built.
364: 
365: The SPA build configuration file can specify the following properties:
366: 
367: - `spaPath` - the URL path which your SPA will be served from.
368: - `apiUrl` - the URL of the OpenMRS backend that your SPA will be communicating with. Defaults to `/openmrs/`.
369: - `configUrls` - an array of URLs pointing to JSON configuration files that will be loaded into your SPA at runtime. These URLs can use template variables like `${openmrsSpaBase}` or `${openmrsBase}` which will be interpolated at runtime using the `interpolateUrl()` function. For example, `${openmrsSpaBase}/config.json` will resolve to `/openmrs/spa/config.json`.
370: - `configPaths` - an array of local JSON configuration files to copy into the build output. The build command appends each copied file's basename to `configUrls`, so the SPA can fetch it at runtime.
371: - `defaultLocale` - the default locale that your SPA will be served in. The app shell build defaults to `en` when no default locale is provided. The Reference Application Docker startup script defaults an empty `SPA_DEFAULT_LOCALE` to `en_GB` (note: uses underscore, not hyphen).
372: - `supportOffline` - boolean value that determines whether or not your SPA will be able to function offline. Defaults to `false`.
373: - `pageTitle` - the default page title that will be used by your SPA. Defaults to `OpenMRS`.
374: - `importmap` - URL or path to the import map (typically `$SPA_PATH/importmap.json`).
375: - `routes` - URL or path to the routes registry (typically `$SPA_PATH/routes.registry.json`).
376: - `env` - the environment string passed to the app shell build. Defaults to `production`.
377: - `assets` - an array of local CSS or JS files to copy into `assets/` in the build output and include in the generated HTML.
378: 
379: **Docker-specific note**: The Reference Application intentionally places placeholders such as `$SPA_PATH`, `$API_URL`, `$SPA_CONFIG_URLS`, and `$SPA_DEFAULT_LOCALE` in `spa-build-config.json`. The CLI treats those as literal strings during `openmrs build`; the generated files still contain those placeholders, and the frontend container replaces them at startup with `startup.sh`.
